prompt: A clear editorial infographic shows a large sentence entering a stylized language model as a stream of individually separated pieces—whole short words, broken word fragments, punctuation marks, and small space symbols—each rendered as numbered tiles; inside the model, the tiles become a sequential ribbon, then emerge as a newly generated ribbon of output tiles forming a response. Beneath, a simple cost meter splits into two labeled columns, “input tokens” for the prompt, document, conversation history, agent notes, and tool-call loops flowing in, and “output tokens” for the generated answer flowing out, with both feeding a single larger gauge labeled “cost to complete the task”; visual callouts show how a huge document, long answer, retries, and repeated agent-tool cycles make the gauge rise, while a small comparison chart of per-token rates sits in the background as useful but secondary information.
